skill.name: ddd-strategic-design
skill.description: Design DDD strategic artifacts including subdomains, bounded contexts, and ubiquitous language for complex business domains.
skill.summary: Create DDD strategic design artifacts for subdomains, bounded contexts, language, and boundary decisions.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to split complex domains without mixing business ownership and implementation concerns. This skill guides DDD strategic design for subdomains, bounded contexts, language, and decisions.
actual_capabilities: Classifies capabilities as core, supporting, or generic subdomains.
Defines bounded contexts around consistency, ownership, and dependencies.
Builds a ubiquitous language glossary with canonical terms and anti-terms.
Frames boundary decisions as ADR-ready rationale before implementation.
Uses the included strategic design template when more structure is needed.
limitations: Does not produce executable code or tactical implementation patterns.
Requires stakeholder input to validate domain facts and business priorities.
Does not replace event storming, discovery workshops, or architecture review.
Needs follow-up tactical design before code changes are planned.

use_cases.title: Split A Monolith
use_cases.description: Map existing capabilities into subdomains and bounded contexts before service extraction.

use_cases.title: Align Product Teams
use_cases.description: Connect ownership boundaries to contexts so teams share clearer responsibilities and language.

use_cases.title: Prepare Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Turn boundary choices into rationale that can be reviewed before implementation starts.

prompt_templates.title: Map A Domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Use @ddd-strategic-design to analyze this domain description. Identify major capabilities, classify subdomains, and list missing stakeholder questions: [domain notes].

prompt_templates.title: Define Bounded Contexts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use @ddd-strategic-design to propose bounded contexts for these capabilities. Include responsibilities, ownership, upstream dependencies, and downstream consumers: [capabilities].

prompt_templates.title: Build Language Glossary
prompt_templates.prompt: Use @ddd-strategic-design to create a ubiquitous language glossary for these teams. Include canonical terms, definitions, context scope, and anti-terms: [terms and conflicts].

prompt_templates.title: Review Boundary Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use @ddd-strategic-design to critique this proposed context map. Identify boundary risks, missing ADRs, ownership gaps, and validation questions: [context map].

output_examples.input: A commerce platform needs clearer boundaries for catalog, pricing, checkout, fulfillment, and billing.
output_examples.output: The skill returns subdomain classifications, candidate bounded contexts, ownership notes, dependency concerns, and decision points for review.

output_examples.input: Two teams use the term order differently during planning.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a glossary entry for each context, highlights conflicting meanings, and recommends canonical language for future decisions.

output_examples.input: A monolith is being split into services before the domain boundaries are agreed.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies boundary risks, asks stakeholder validation questions, and suggests ADR topics before implementation proceeds.

best_practices: Bring real stakeholder language and examples before asking for boundaries.
Validate every proposed context with ownership, consistency, and dependency constraints.
Record boundary decisions before converting the model into tactical design.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a substitute for business discovery.
Treating bounded contexts as service names without checking consistency boundaries.
Skipping glossary conflicts because current terms seem obvious.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It produces strategic design artifacts and guidance for architecture planning.

faq.question: Can it help split a monolith?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps classify capabilities and propose boundaries before technical extraction starts.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Use domain notes, capability lists, team responsibilities, terminology conflicts, and known business constraints.

faq.question: Does it replace domain experts?
faq.answer: No. Stakeholders must validate the model, language, and business priorities.

faq.question: What artifacts does it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce subdomain tables, bounded context catalogs, glossary terms, and boundary decision rationale.

faq.question: Is it useful after implementation starts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review boundary drift, ownership gaps, and language conflicts in existing systems.
